title: The ordinary termwise adjunct of a single-complex map
statement: Let $C,D$ be abelian categories, $L:C\to D$ and $R:D\to C$ additive functors with an adjunction $\eta:\mathrm{id}_C\to R\circ L$, let $A\in C$ and let $J$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex in $D$. For a chain map $c:(LA)[0]\to J$, define $\operatorname{adj}_0(c):A[0]\to R(J)$ to be $\mathrm{single}(\eta_A)\gg\rho_{LA}^{-1}\gg R(c)$, where $\rho:R(\mathrm{single}(-))\cong\mathrm{single}(R(-))$ is the canonical single-complex comparison. This is the explicit ordinary termwise adjunct. Its data is this composite of already constructed chain maps; no existence theorem is used to choose it.

source.place: Tag 0DVC, pre-derived adjoint functors: the ordinary adjunction unit on complexes; also the termwise adjunct in Tag 072W.

proof.text: Compose the single of the adjunction unit with the inverse single-complex comparison for R and the image of c. Each factor is a chain map, so their categorical composite supplies the data and all chain-map laws. Its displayed equation is reflexivity after unfolding. In degree zero this is the ordinary adjunction unit formula; for zero c the composite is zero. No derived category or choice of resolution is involved.
